note: Computes the required output size for the Montgomery reduction result. This is 2*p_words+2 words, which is what bigint_monty_redc expects.
Copies the input x into z. The size of z is the size of x, which may be smaller than output_size.
When n <= capacity, resizes to capacity. But capacity may be less than n if the vector was previously shrunk, causing z.size() to remain below output_size.
When n > capacity, rounds up to a multiple of 8. This is the implicit rounding that may not reach 2*p_words+2 if p_words is not a multiple of 4.

code: bigint_monty_redc(z.mutable_data(), m_p.data(), m_p_words, m_p_dash, ws.data(), ws.size());
note: Passes z's data pointer to bigint_monty_redc, which assumes z has at least 2*p_words+2 words. If grow_to did not allocate enough, this writes out of bounds.
Computes the required size of z as 2*p_size+2. This is the size that z must have for the reduction to be safe.
Iterates over z starting at offset i. The inner loop accesses z_i[j] for j up to z_size-i-1, so the maximum index accessed is z_size-1.
Writes to z at index i+j. If z was not grown to at least z_size words, this write goes out of bounds, causing a heap buffer overflow.
